abstract: Temporal prediction is thought to draw on two subcortical structures: the basal ganglia for the periodic beat, and the cerebellum for the aperiodic interval. Lesion, imaging and electrophysiological studies converge on this division, yet each tests it within a single modality and task, leaving its generality unknown. We developed a battery of timing tasks for multi-task fMRI, densely sampling 31 non-clinical adults in every combination of temporal structure, sensory modality and task. Encoding engaged the same cortico-striatal-cerebellar architecture throughout. Within it, the dorsal striatum was uniquely selective for the production task. Pooled across tasks, it responded more to auditory beat than interval sequences, whereas the cerebellum did not distinguish them. Yet, removing regularity did not lower that response: the preference is for the beat, not for predictability. Temporal prediction therefore draws on a shared architecture whose striatal node is context-dependent: tuned to periodic time, and to time turned into action.
